research_question: Identify gaps in methods and evidence for cyber criminal profiling, with emphasis on human factors aspects.
scope_notes: No date or language filters were applied. Search terms are in English. Document types are not restricted and will vary by database. Fielded searches target title, abstract, and keywords where the database supports this; OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar use full-record text matching. Results should be screened following PRISMA/SoK guidance.

queries.crossref: cybercrime cybercriminal criminal profiling human factors psychology

rationale: The strategy models the topic with three orthogonal blocks: (1) the actor/behavior type (cybercriminal, hacker, malicious insider), (2) the analytical frame (profiling, offender profiling, behavioral/psychological characterization), and (3) the human-factor angle (psychological, personality, cognitive, motivational, decision-making, and psychosocial dimensions). The profiling and human-factor blocks are intentionally broad in order not to pre-judge what counts as a human factor or as profiling during screening. Explicit gap-related terms such as 'gap*' or 'research needs' are omitted because articles seldom use these words in a consistent way; gaps are identified during full-text screening rather than by search filtering.
limitations: The search will not retrieve all relevant items: Crossref cannot express boolean logic, so the Crossref query is only an approximation. ACM and arXiv do not reliably support the same wildcard operators, so morphological variants were expanded, but some uncommon forms may still be missed. Terms cover English-language vocabulary and may not find works using non-English constructs. Because the search focuses on title, abstract, and keyword fields in most databases, studies that mention profiling or human factors only in the full text may be missed. The broad human-factor terms can also introduce false positives from cyber-security usability or user-centered design research, which will require manual screening. Finally, the strategy does not enumerate all cybercrime subtypes (e.g., state-sponsored actors, organized cybercrime, darknet vendors, specific fraud types), so additional supplementary searches may be needed for those sub-populations.
